THE DAY'S SHAPE: yields are EASING for the first time this week. The ten-year gilt is down to 5.38%
from 5.4147% and the US ten-year down to 5.23% from 5.255%, after a run that took the thirty-year to
its highest since 2004. Sterling firmer at 1.3250, gold flat, oil up slightly, bitcoin down 0.6%.

A PARTIAL CNBC FAILURE, WORTH RECORDING: the first multi-symbol request returned NULL for Brent (all
three contracts), euro-sterling, the gilt and the VIX while returning good data for FTSE, the S&P,
sterling, gold, bitcoin and the US ten-year. Re-requesting the failed symbols in two smaller groups
returned all of them correctly. So a null from this endpoint is not a market state; it is a partial
response, and the fix is to re-request in smaller batches rather than to assume the instrument is not
trading. This matters because a null on @LCO.1 on expiry day could easily be misread as the roll.
